title: A Modest Proposal to Rein in Sports Gambling | Institute for Family Studies
gist: Public Discourse teaser carried by IFS: Joshua Sohn proposes a populist 'non-discrimination' mandate for sportsbooks, which currently limit savvy bettors, as a light-touch way to rein in harmful online sports gambling.

insights.claim: Online sports gambling is draining finances and harming the prospects of young men, yet politicians avoid cracking down because they fear being seen as Puritans and antagonizing millions of bettor voters.
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: Regulatory inertia means the sector keeps growing; policy risk for sportsbooks is low near term absent a populist angle.
insights.locator: It’s no secret that online sports gambling is a serious problem

insights.claim: Joshua Sohn proposes Congress mandate that sportsbooks not discriminate and treat all customers on equal terms, because sportsbooks radically limit bets from known savvy gamblers who can exploit inefficient lines.
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: A non-discrimination mandate would remove a key sportsbook profit protection (limiting winners) and could cut margins; the idea is only a proposal in a teaser.
insights.locator: Congress should mandate that sportsbooks not discriminate
